### Selected pod / cluster

Click any pod or controller node in the graph above: a pod exports its own name, a controller exports all of its child pod names — both cases also export the resolved cluster name. A sibling log panel (e.g. Loki/ClickHouse) can filter on `${selected_pod}` and `${cluster_sel}`.

selected_pod: `${selected_pod}`

cluster_sel: `${cluster_sel}`

### Alert pod list / alert names (exported)

This backend demo's seed fixture (`dev/victoriametrics/topology.prom`) has no alert data contract, so `alert_pod_list` and `alert_names` always resolve to `$__empty` here — this is a documented seed-data limitation, not a panel fault. See the **KSG Showcase** dashboard (`ksg-switch-demo`, inline fixture) for a working example with real alert-carrying nodes (`mongo-2`, `mesh-gateway-0`, `worker-1`, `data-mongo-2`).

alert_pod_list: `${alert_pod_list}`

alert_names: `${alert_names}`

query.uql: parse-json | scope "elements.nodes" | project "namespace"="data.labels.namespace" | summarize by "namespace" | order by "namespace" asc
parse-json | scope "elements.nodes" | project "name"="data.name" | summarize by "name" | order by "name" asc

list.name: alert_pod_list
list.label: Alert pod list (exported)
list.description: Written by the KSG panel after each graph load — pod names that currently have at least one alert (any severity); $__empty means a loaded graph with zero alerting pods. custom + multi + allowCustomValue so it can carry the multi-value writes this produces — a plain textbox variable cannot hold multiple values. This backend demo's seed fixture (dev/victoriametrics/topology.prom) has no alert data contract, so this variable is always $__empty here — see the ksg-switch-demo dashboard (inline fixture) for a working example with real alert data (mesh-gateway-0, mongo-2).

list.name: alert_names
list.label: Alert names (exported)
list.description: Written by the KSG panel after each graph load — distinct alert names found across all node kinds (pod/node/pvc/service/controller), any severity; $__empty means zero alerts in the loaded graph. custom + multi + allowCustomValue for the same reason as alert_pod_list. This backend demo's seed fixture (dev/victoriametrics/topology.prom) has no alert data contract, so this variable is always $__empty here — see the ksg-switch-demo dashboard (inline fixture) for a working example with real alert data (~12 distinct alert names).

list.name: selected_pod
list.label: Selected pod
list.description: Written by the KSG panel on left-click of a pod (single name) or controller (all child pod names), regardless of status. custom + multi + allowCustomValue so it can hold pod-name value(s) outside any fixed option list — a plain textbox variable cannot carry the multi-value writes a controller click produces. Consume from a sibling log panel, e.g. ${selected_pod:lucene}. $__empty means nothing selected yet.

list.name: cluster_sel
list.label: Selected cluster
list.description: Written by the KSG panel alongside selected_pod on pod/controller click — the resolved cluster name. custom + multi + allowCustomValue (multi is normally unused since a click resolves to a single cluster; kept for shape consistency with selected_pod). Consume from a sibling log panel, e.g. ${cluster_sel:lucene}. $__empty means unresolved/nothing selected.
